wave_definitions.0: Small isolated fixes and UI work — fits inside one existing domain, no new contract, no schema/migration.
wave_definitions.1: Features fitting existing stable domain boundaries — may touch one domain's internals but no cross-domain contract needed.
wave_definitions.2: Features requiring exactly one new public contract.
wave_definitions.4: High-risk AI, imaging, official integrations, privacy/security-automation, or storage work — requires the most caution regardless of contract count.

feature_intake_checklist.instruction: Assign exactly one domain code from domain_taxonomy_reference. If none fits, mark OUT_OF_DOMAIN_TAXONOMY and route to F2-PREP-001 for taxonomy review before intake proceeds.

Identify which Prisma model(s) the feature reads/writes and confirm their primary owner per F0-003_MODULE_OWNERSHIP_EVIDENCE.md §3. A feature may not write another domain's model directly (DEPENDENCY_MAP.md §6).
State clinic-scoped / organization-scoped / platform-global and name the enforcing helper (clinicScope.ts / tenantGuard.ts / clinicAccess.ts) the route will use.
List every contract this feature consumes from another domain. If the needed contract does not exist yet, the feature is SAFE_AFTER_CONTRACT at best, not SAFE_NOW.
Confirm the feature does not read/write another domain's Prisma model directly and does not import another domain's internal service/route file (DEPENDENCY_MAP.md §3).
State whether a Prisma migration is needed; if destructive, require an expand-migrate-contract plan, not a single-step change.

State whether the change needs an AuditLog/ActivityLog entry (core, clearly bounded) and, if it touches consent, whether it needs the separate consent-audit path (RISK_REGISTER R-047 flags a possible duplicate-audit-concept risk here — do not invent a third audit mechanism).
Classify KVKK sensitivity (LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH) and check against KVKK_ARCHITECTURE_FREEZE_BOUNDARY.md §2/§3 before any schema or consent-adjacent change is authorized.
Confirm the route/service enforces existing auth middleware + role/permission checks (utils/roles.ts pattern); do not invent a parallel authorization mechanism.
If the feature needs async work, state that no general-purpose queue exists yet (ADR-006/007 NEEDS_POC) — only PM2 cron + JobLock are available today; do not assume BullMQ or any unselected platform.

If the feature calls an external provider (WhatsApp/SMS/Instagram/AI/imaging bridge/future official adapter), confirm it stays inside that channel's own bespoke provider-factory pattern (no shared AI Gateway or Integration Platform exists yet — MODULE_MAP.md 'Planned / Not Implemented').
Name the test file(s) and whether they need the disposable-Postgres/MinIO runtime (scripts/test-runtime/, F1-003-P2) or run DB-free.

State whether the change is a normal PM2/bare-VPS deploy (current topology, ADR-016) or needs anything else; no containerization/orchestration change is authorized without an independently evidenced trigger.

State the exact rollback path. Additive/reversible code changes: standard git revert. Any schema change: must have an expand-migrate-contract path, since RISK_REGISTER/DEPENDENCY_MAP evidence (F0-011-P2) shows `_prisma_migrations` bookkeeping does not self-reconcile after a physical rollback.

State the minimum safe, non-activating production check (per the R-061/KVKK-HIGH-006/008 precedent in RISK_REGISTER.md) before the feature is claimed production-verified; do not claim production readiness from agent self-testing alone.
